fields.description:
## Context

Our LLM re-review trigger word collides with the EXTERNAL CI ChatOps matcher we do not own
(lfit/releng-gerrit_to_platform). `infra/gerrit/gerrit_to_platform.ini.template` maps
`recheck = verify` under `[mapping "comment-added"]`, and g2p's comment matcher is
substring-based, so a comment containing the retired LLM word (which embeds `recheck`)
ALSO dispatches the Verified workflow — cancelling an in-flight CI run and leaving a
`Verified -1` that reflects a cancellation, not a failure (observed on changes 1551 and 1577).

Our own matcher (`src/rebar/review_bot/retrigger.py`) is already whole-word safe; the
collision is entirely on the CI side, which we cannot change. OPERATOR DECISION (option c,
2026-08-12): RENAME our trigger. HARD CUTOVER, no deprecation window — keeping the old word
alive keeps the collision alive. The retired word gets a clear refusal reply naming the new
trigger.

Additional finding from triage: the bot's OWN reply texts (`_ACCEPTED_MESSAGE` and
`_refusal_message`) currently embed the retired word verbatim. Those are posted as Gerrit
comments, so the bot's replies are themselves a live source of spurious CI dispatch. Any
text the bot posts must be scrubbed too, not just the matcher.

## Design

New trigger token: **`rerun-llm-review`**.

Chosen because it contains no `[mapping "comment-added"]` key from the ini template as a
substring (the only key is `recheck`), no ini key contains it, and it names both the
mechanism (rerun) and the gate (llm-review) so it cannot be confused with CI's `recheck`.
The substring-safety property is pinned by a test that PARSES the ini template rather than
hardcoding `recheck`, so adding a future CI ChatOps mapping that collides fails the suite.

Changes:
- `retrigger.py`: `TRIGGER_TOKEN = "rerun-llm-review"`, `_TOKEN_RE` matched on the new word
  with the same `-`/`_`-binding word boundaries. Add `_RETIRED_TOKEN_RE` for the old word.
- Handler order (each earlier check sees strictly less attacker-controlled input):
  loop guard -> new-token match -> retired-token match (refusal branch) -> project guard ->
  eligibility -> reset. The retired branch NEVER enqueues a review and NEVER writes a label;
  it posts exactly one best-effort `post_comment` refusal and returns `None`.
- The retired-word refusal, the findings refusal, and the accepted reply must all be free of
  every ini-mapped trigger word. The retired-word refusal therefore refers to the old trigger
  descriptively ("the former LLM re-review trigger word") instead of spelling it, since
  spelling it would re-dispatch CI from our own comment.
- Docs/guides/runbooks/comments updated to the new word.

Out of scope (explicitly): `infra/gerrit/gerrit_to_platform.ini.template`. The `recheck`
mapping stays as-is; it is CI's word.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — A `rerun-llm-review` comment drives the existing accepted path (eligibility ->
      fixed-neutral reset -> forced review event), and near-miss forms
      (`rerun-llm-reviews`, `pre-rerun-llm-review`, `rerun-llm-review-x`) remain silent
      no-ops.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_review_bot_retrigger.py -q`
- [ ] AC2 — A comment carrying the retired word never returns a review event, never resets a
      vote, and posts exactly one refusal reply that names `rerun-llm-review`.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit -q -k "retrigger or recheck"`
- [ ] AC3 — No text the bot posts to Gerrit (accepted reply, findings refusal, retired-word
      refusal) contains any `[mapping "comment-added"]` key parsed from
      `infra/gerrit/gerrit_to_platform.ini.template`.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit -q -k "retrigger or recheck"`
- [ ] AC4 — `TRIGGER_TOKEN` contains no ini-mapped comment-added trigger key as a substring,
      and no ini key contains `TRIGGER_TOKEN`; the assertion reads the ini template at test
      time rather than hardcoding the word.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit -q -k "retrigger or recheck"`
- [ ] AC5 — Contributor-facing documentation instructs the new word only; no doc, guide, or
      runbook still tells a contributor to comment the retired word.
      Verify: `grep -rn "recheck-review" docs/ src/rebar/_guides/ AGENTS.md CONTRIBUTING.md infra/`
      returns no hit outside the historical ADR record.
- [ ] AC5b — The retired word survives in `src/rebar/` ONLY inside the retired-token detector
      (the regex and the module docstring line that explains it), never as an instruction.
      Verify: `grep -rn "recheck-review" src/rebar/ | grep -v "_RETIRED_TOKEN_RE"` returns no
      line that instructs a contributor to comment it.
- [ ] AC6 — Gates are green.
      Verify: `make lint && make typecheck && python -m pytest tests/interfaces -q -k "review_bot or retrigger"`
